questions.prompt: A permits service used by 40 city agencies, each seeing only its own applications. Tick what v1 needs.

options.label: Sign-in with roles per agency
options.why: Every request has to know who and which agency before anything else.

options.label: Row-level permissions on applications
options.why: Isolation enforced in the database, so a missed check in the app can't leak another agency's rows.

options.label: Append-only audit log
options.why: Public-sector work: who changed what, and when, gets asked for.

options.label: Workflow states for an application
options.why: Submitted, in review, approved, rejected: the product is the workflow.

options.label: A separate database per agency
options.why: 40 databases to migrate and back up. Row-level security isolates without it; split out later if one agency needs it.

options.label: One search cluster across all agencies
options.why: A shared index is the easiest place to leak across tenants. Postgres search is enough for v1.

options.label: Real-time collaborative editing
options.why: Nobody asked for it. Locking an application while it's in review is enough.

questions.prompt: Match each component to its job.

pairs.right: Checks the sign-in and rate-limits each agency
Absorbs bursts between intake and processing
Do the slow steps and scale with queue depth
Stores applications and keeps agencies apart
Records who did what, and never changes

questions.why: The split is about failure: if the workers fall behind, intake still takes applications.

questions.prompt: One agency reports that submitting an application went from 300 ms to 4 s since this morning. Put your first moves in order.
items: Check whether it's one agency or all of them
Look at what changed in that window: deploys, config, flags, data size
Trace one slow request end to end
Form one hypothesis and test it
Fix or roll back, then confirm on the same metric
questions.why: Scope first, then the change, then the evidence. Rolling back before you know the scope can hide the cause.
